name: Capacitance dilatometry (thermal expansion and magnetostriction) of thin single crystals in a PPMS, 2-50 K, up to 9 T
plain_name: Measure how a thin crystal shrinks or stretches on cooling and in a magnetic field
description: Mount a sub-500 um thin crystal in the slot of a miniature capacitance dilatometer integrated into a Quantum Design PPMS and record the relative length change from 2 to 50 K (alpha(T) by 0.1 K interval differentiation) in zero field and in 9 T; the cell can be rotated in situ.
keywords: Measure how a thin crystal shrinks or stretches on cooling and in a magnetic field

sources.citation: R. Küchler, S. Panja, S. Wirth, P. Gegenwart, 'High-Resolution Capacitance Dilatometry of Microscopically Thin Samples Using a Miniature Dilatometer', arXiv:2601.13231 (2026)

requirements.rationale: alpha(T) of the AgCrS2 crystal was determined over 2-50 K.
Thermal expansion was compared at zero field and 9 T.
The length change is read as a capacitance, so electrical leads to the dilatometer cell on the sample stage are required.

confirmation_note: Requirements taken from the cited procedure and independently re-verified against the source (research/v4, 2026-11-01). Users must confirm them for their own run; edits require confirmation again.
